title: A protocol for mimicking lipid-mediated phase separation on the membrane using giant unilamellar vesicles
protocol: Design the primers for the Ago1-GFP fusion gene using SnapGene software.
Include 15 bases of the pET28a plasmid in Primer Ago1-F for recombination.
Ensure Primer Ago1-R contains at least 15 bases of GFP for recombination.
Include 15 bases of the pET28a plasmid in Primer GFP-R for recombination.
Prepare two 50 μL PCR reaction mixes in PCR tubes to amplify Ago1 and GFP, respectively.
Purify the PCR products using the Vazyme gel purification kit.
Recombine the purified PCR products with EcoR1/Xho1-digested pET28a plasmid.
Transform Escherichia coli DH5α with the recombination mixture.
Pick a single colony and grow it in 1 mL of Luria–Bertani (LB) medium.
Culture the LB at 37°C for 5–6 h.
Take 1 μL LB as a template and run PCR to identify positive clones.
Sequence to confirm the plasmid.
Extract the plasmid with FastPure EndoFree Plasmid Maxi Kit.
Transform E. coli BL21 with the pET28a plasmid for bacterial expression of His-tagged fusion Ago1-GFP protein.
Pick a single colony and grow it in 5 mL of LB medium containing 100 μg/mL kanamycin.
Incubate at 37°C with shaking at 250 rpm.
Dilute the overnight culture with 250 mL of fresh LB medium containing 100 μg/mL kanamycin and continue shaking at 37°C until OD600nm = 0.6 (∼3–5 h).
Add 1 mM IPTG and shake for an additional 16 h at 16°C to induce Ago1-GFP protein expression.
Collect the cells by centrifuging for 10 min at 15,000 × g at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the bacterial cell pellet in 40 mL of lysis buffer.
Sonicate the cells at 40% power using 5 s on/5 s off for 15–25 min.
Centrifuge the lysate at 15,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 50 mL tube.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.45 μm filter.
Add 300 μL of Ni beads to a column.
Wash the beads with 10 mL of H2O.
Wash the beads with 10 mL of binding buffer.
Add the lysate to the column.
Incubate to allow binding between the His-tagged protein and the Ni beads.
Wash the beads three times with 10 mL of washing buffer.
Elute the protein with elution buffer.
Separate the sample on SDS-PAGE.
Stain with Coomassie blue G-250 to check the protein quality and quantity.
Ultrafiltration or dialysis to remove imidazole.
Dissolve phospholipids or lipids in chloroform.
Weigh 2.4 mg of DOPC and dissolve it in 3 mL of chloroform to make a 0.8 mg/mL solution.
Weigh 2.2 mg of DPPC and dissolve it in 3 mL of chloroform to make a 0.73 mg/mL solution.
Weigh 1.2 mg of cholesterol with a Micro-Analysis Balance in 3 mL of chloroform to make a 0.4 mg/mL solution.
Dissolve 0.1 mg of PI(4,5)P2 in 1.33 mL of chloroform to make a 0.075 mg/mL solution.
Mix the lipids in the amounts shown in Table 5, with the weight ratio of DOPC: DPPC: Cholesterol: PI(4,5)P2 being 36:23:6:6.
Vortex the mixture to fully mix.
Remove chloroform by blowing clean nitrogen (purity 99.999%) and further dry with nitrogen for at least 40 min.
Add 200 μL of growth buffer and incubate for 1 h at 60°C in the drying oven.
Transfer the GUV to a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube after incubation.
Centrifuge the GUV sample at 100 × g for 10 min at room temperature to remove aggregated lipid species.
Incubate the purified protein with the GUVs to make the protein phase separation on the membrane.
Remove the protein from −80°C storage and place it on ice to allow the sample to thaw slowly.
Transfer the mixture immediately to a glass cell culture dish.
Cover the dish with a square coverslip.
Seal the coverslip with nail polish to prevent liquid evaporation.
Set up the microscope.
Locate GUVs using the 10 × objective first.
Change to the 40 × oil objective and add immersion oil.
Click the Locate tab to find GUVs through the eyepiece.
Go to the Acquisition mode and click Smart Setup button.
Select channels needed (mainly 555 nm and 488 nm).
Choose Airyscan, SNR/Sensitivity, and smartest line capture module.
Highlight a single track in Channels window.
Set Laser Power initially to 0.4%.
Increase laser power if detector gain cannot achieve desired intensity.
Adjust Master Gain up to 850 V under the Airyscan module.
Decrease the Digital Offset to reduce the background signal.
Increase the Digital Gain to amplify all signals and background.
Adjust the scanning parameters.
Go to the Acquisition Mode window.
Select a suitable area and zoom setting to capture an area of interest.
Use the Crop button to adjust the desired field of view after stopping a Live image.
Select a Frame Size to represent the desired area per pixel, typically 1024 × 1024.
Adjust the Scan speed to 9 for a quick scan speed.
Select Bidirectional scanning mode.
Select a value for Averaging to improve image quality, usually 2–4 is sufficient.
Select the dynamic range with the Bits per Pixel setting, typically eight-bit is enough.
Click the Snap button to acquire a single frame.
Go to the Z-stack window and select the preferred scanning mode; use First/Last mode.
Select the Live button, use the focus knob to locate one end of the specimen, then click the Set First button.
Focus on another end of the specimen, then click the Set Last button.
Set the Interval to define the step size of the Z-stack; use the value from the Optimal button for best 3D reconstruction.
Go to the Time-Series window and set the Duration and Interval values.
Find a GUV that contains phase-separated proteins.
Start imaging by clicking the Start Experiment button.
Files are processed by Airyscan and saved in .czi format.
Open the Imaris software.
Open Imaris 9.0.1 by double-clicking the software icon on the desktop.
Open the Z-stack file in Imaris using "Ctrl+O" or by dragging the file to the software.
Click the 3D View button to view the file in three dimensions.
Drag the file by clicking the left mouse button to access the 3D view of the GUV.
Create a new surface reconstruction by clicking on Add new surface in the top left corner.
Choose the channel and set Surface Details and Background Subtraction.
Select the channel you want to reconstruct.
Set the Surfaces Detail and Background Subtraction.
Measure distances by left-clicking on the image in slice view.
Set the measured distance as the background subtraction.
Click on either the blue or green arrow at the bottom to finish the surface reconstruction.
Ensure you are satisfied with the reconstruction by dragging and zooming in and out.
Select/unselect the fluorescence channels and the reconstructed surfaces to check for sufficient overlap.
If refinement is needed, start over from step 1.
If you are satisfied with the result, export the image by clicking Store As.
Open the 3D/time-lapse file in Imaris 9.0.1.
Click the Animation button to view dynamic changes of phase-separated proteins.
Press the left mouse button to see different slices changing over time.
Create a new surface reconstruction.
Set an appropriate Surface Detail value to avoid long reconstruction times or crashes.
Find the Preferences tab and click the Display button to change the background color to white for better visualization.
Click the Snapshot button to export the movie.
Click the red round button to start exporting the movie in .mp4 format.
Choose a compression factor of 0, higher quality, and a frame rate set to 10 frames per second.
Select the original resolution ratio for the movie size.
Click the save button to export the movie.
Choose the value to check, selecting volume.
Identify and list all objects’ volume information.
Select objects for analysis by clicking on them in the statistics list.
Observe changes in object volume over time in the viewing area.
Export statistics by clicking on the Export Statistics tab.
Save the file to a chosen location.
Use Imaris-generated data files with Excel or Graphpad prism.
